answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. The protocol records stake per identity and penalizes proven fraud, so splitting one operator across many keys does not create free influence: every new identity needs another deposit, and each can lose it. A delta in reputation can reflect verified work, while a harbor of trusted peers helps review disputes; the tide of new accounts cannot cheaply wash out that history.
